subject.title: fix(auth): expired OAuth credentials survive per-provider credential discovery and silently break background operations

question: Should provider-level background discovery discard expired OAuth entries, or must it resolve them through the same refresh-capable, profile-aware path used by normal auth resolution?
rationale: Current OpenClaw OAuth resolution explicitly refreshes selected credentials, while this PR makes expiry terminal before that resolver is reached; deciding whether background discovery may intentionally fail closed is a compatibility contract choice.

options.title: Use profile-aware resolution
options.body: Route provider-level background discovery through the ordered OAuth/profile resolver so refresh, preference, and profile selection remain consistent.

options.title: Keep the fail-closed guard
options.body: Accept that automatic operations require a still-valid OAuth access token and document/test the OAuth-only unavailable-auth outcome.

recommendation.title: Use profile-aware resolution
recommendation.body: Route provider-level background discovery through the ordered OAuth/profile resolver so refresh, preference, and profile selection remain consistent.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work spans both auth-profile ordering/failover and OAuth refresh-token persistence.
